# quartodown <picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="man/figures/logo.png" /><img src="man/figures/logo-light.png" align="right" height="139" alt="quartodown logo" /></picture>

quartodown is an R package that turns your package's README, help pages and
vignettes into a website, rendered entirely by [Quarto](https://quarto.org/).

## Why quartodown?

Every page, help pages included, is a Quarto page, so you get:

- every Quarto feature, from callouts and tabsets to code annotations and
  cross-references, on every page;
- Quarto's themes, extensions and settings.

On top of that, quartodown adds:

- the package website layout R users know from pkgdown: a home page sidebar, a
  grouped function reference, articles and a changelog;
- function links with hover tooltips.

## Installation

Install the stable version from CRAN:

```r
install.packages("quartodown")
```

or the development version from GitHub:

```r
pak::pak("BjarkeHautop/quartodown")
```

quartodown also needs [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) installed.

## Usage

[Browse the site](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/quartodown/) to see how it
looks! [Quarto
features](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/quartodown/vignettes/articles/showcase.html)
shows callouts, tabsets, footnotes and more on a quartodown site. If you like
what you see, and want to use it for your own package, run:

```r
quartodown::use_quartodown()
```

This writes `_quartodown/_quartodown.yml`, with a `reference:` field that lists
your package's current functions in one section; edit it to group them however
you'd like. It also gitignores the files the build generates.

If your package already has a pkgdown site, most of `_pkgdown.yml` can be copied
over as is; see [Coming from
pkgdown](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/quartodown/vignettes/customizing.html#coming-from-pkgdown).

Then build the site:

```r
quartodown::build_site()
```

In an interactive session, this also opens the site in your browser.

To publish it on GitHub Pages, run `quartodown::use_quartodown_action()`. It
writes a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the site on every push and deploys
it to the `gh-pages` branch.

See
[Customizing](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/quartodown/vignettes/customizing.html)
for everything `_quartodown.yml` can configure.
